skill.name: wp-performance
skill.description: Diagnose and improve WordPress performance with backend-only profiling, WP-CLI checks, Query Monitor headers, Server-Timing, and safe verification guidance.
skill.summary: Diagnose WordPress performance bottlenecks with backend-only profiling and safe verification.
skill.author: Automattic

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown command examples, URLs, and diagnostic guidance. The helper script does run WP-CLI through Node child_process and checks files under a provided WordPress path. The main remaining concern is wp profile eval, which can execute PHP in the target site context.

remediation.issue: WP-CLI execution in the helper script
remediation.suggestion: Document that perf_inspect.mjs runs local WP-CLI commands and require explicit user confirmation before execution, especially in production.

remediation.issue: Potential PHP execution through wp profile eval guidance
remediation.suggestion: Add guardrails for wp profile eval, prohibit untrusted snippets, and require approval before eval-based profiling.
Keep installs, cache flushes, debug changes, and load tests behind explicit approval. Prefer read-only checks by default.

content.value_statement: Slow WordPress pages can hide problems in queries, cron, cache, or remote calls. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through backend-only measurement and safe verification.
actual_capabilities: Creates a backend-only profiling plan using WP-CLI, Server-Timing, Query Monitor, and logs.
Runs or guides a deterministic perf_inspect report when WP-CLI is available.
Checks autoloaded option size and known cache drop-ins.
Maps slow symptoms to database, cache, cron, or HTTP API fixes.
Defines repeatable verification steps before and after changes.
limitations: Requires shell or WP-CLI access for most diagnostics.
Does not replace load testing, APM traces, or browser lab measurements.
Some commands need explicit approval in production environments.
Results depend on stable test URLs, user state, and cache conditions.

use_cases.title: Triage Slow Page Loads
use_cases.description: Find the likely backend cause of high TTFB with repeatable measurements and safe next checks.

use_cases.title: Review Production Readiness
use_cases.description: Check autoloaded options, debug constants, cache drop-ins, and WP-CLI doctor signals before release.

use_cases.title: Plan Cache And Query Fixes
use_cases.description: Turn profiling output into focused database, object cache, cron, or HTTP API remediation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Check A Slow URL
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage with a known symptom.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the WordPress performance skill to investigate [URL] on [environment]. Ask me before write operations and produce a baseline-first plan.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze WP-CLI Signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this perf_inspect output and identify the most likely bottleneck. Recommend safe next checks and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Profile A Multisite Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan backend-only profiling for [site URL] in a multisite install. Include WP-CLI targeting, Query Monitor headers, and cache controls.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare before and after measurements for [change]. Prioritize database, cache, cron, and HTTP API fixes with rollback guidance.

output_examples.input: A logged-out product page has high TTFB after a plugin release.
output: Baseline the same URL with warmed cache and repeated samples.
Check profiling stages and hook hotspots for the released plugin.
Inspect Query Monitor REST data for duplicate queries or slow HTTP calls.
Verify any fix with the same URL, user state, and cache state.

output_examples.input: A site has large autoloaded options and intermittent admin slowness.
output: Measure total autoloaded option size before changing storage.
Identify the largest options and confirm whether each is still used.
Move large computed data to non-autoloaded storage or cache.
Repeat the measurement and check logs for regressions.

output_examples.input: Checkout is slow when an external service has high latency.
output: Confirm whether remote HTTP calls happen during the request path.
Add timeouts, caching, batching, or asynchronous processing where appropriate.
Measure the same checkout path before and after the change.

best_practices: Capture baseline metrics before changing code, plugins, cache, or configuration.
Run production-impacting diagnostics only after explicit approval.
Verify each fix with the same URL, user state, and cache conditions.
anti_patterns: Flushing all caches during traffic without confirming scope and impact.
Enabling debug or query tools in production without approval.
Changing multiple bottleneck areas before measuring the first result.

faq.question: Does this skill need browser access?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for backend-only workflows using WP-CLI, HTTP headers, logs, and REST responses.

faq.question: Can it run commands on my server?
faq.answer: Yes, when you approve that workflow. The helper script uses WP-CLI and should be treated as local command execution.

faq.question: Is it safe for production sites?
faq.answer: Use read-only checks first. Require explicit approval before installs, cache flushes, debug changes, or load tests.

faq.question: What bottlenecks can it investigate?
faq.answer: It covers database queries, autoloaded options, object cache, cron, remote HTTP calls, and backend profiling signals.

faq.question: Does it replace APM or load testing?
faq.answer: No. It complements APM, profilers, and load tests by organizing backend diagnostics and verification steps.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
